exposure: OB-GYN practice patterns for eclampsia prevention
OB-GYN experiences with magnesium sulfate complications
Clinical scenarios (preeclampsia with contraindications to magnesium)
outcome: Proportion of OB-GYNs administering alternative antiepileptics for preeclampsia with contraindications
Proportion of OB-GYNs administering magnesium sulfate at usual/reduced dose or no antiepileptic for pulmonary edema complicating preeclampsia
Proportion of OB-GYNs administering magnesium sulfate at reduced dose for renal compromise complicating preeclampsia
Proportion of OB-GYNs encountering magnesium toxicity complications
Knowledge of magnesium toxicity symptoms and dosing
Perceived demand for dedicated personnel with continuous magnesium infusions
Endorsement for an alternative antiepileptic to magnesium
cohort: The study participants were 564 practicing OB-GYNs in the Pregnancy-Related Care Research Network who completed a web-based survey.
finding: The study found wide variation in OB-GYN practices for eclampsia prevention, with many using alternative antiepileptics or supporting the need for new alternatives due to concerns about magnesium sulfate safety and side effects.
